note: 中文译文按课文语境自译，课本原文无中文对照，仅供跟读理解参考

items.en: Wang Mei is at Li Lin’s house.
items.zh: 王梅在李琳家。

items.en: Li Lin’s grandpa takes a box out from his bedroom.
items.zh: 李琳的爷爷从卧室里拿出一个盒子。

items.en: Thank you for inviting me over to see your collection, Grandpa Li!
items.zh: 李爷爷，谢谢您邀请我来看您的收藏！

items.en: You’re welcome!
items.zh: 不客气！

items.en: Let’s start with these stamps.
items.zh: 我们先从这些邮票看起吧。

items.en: This one shows that ancient Chinese people used shells as a form of money.
items.zh: 这一张说明古代中国人用贝壳作为一种货币。

items.en: Think of the Chinese character “贩”.
items.zh: 想想汉字“贩”。

items.en: Oh!
items.zh: 哦！

items.en: It includes a “shell”.
items.zh: 它里面包含一个“贝”。

items.en: These stamps represent different types of ancient Chinese currency.
items.zh: 这些邮票代表中国古代不同种类的货币。

items.en: Some ancient money was in the shape of a knife or spade.
items.zh: 有些古钱币是刀形或铲形的。

items.en: In 221 BCE, Qinshihuang unified China and introduced round coins with a square hole in the centre.
items.zh: 公元前221年，秦始皇统一中国，推出了中间有方孔的圆形硬币。

items.en: Later on, round coins became the main type of money.
items.zh: 后来，圆形硬币成为主要的货币形式。

items.en: That’s cool!
items.zh: 太酷了！

items.en: They look really old.
items.zh: 它们看起来真的很古老。

items.en: They are indeed very old!
items.zh: 它们确实非常古老！

items.en: What about paper money?
items.zh: 那纸币呢？

items.en: Paper money has a long history in China.
items.zh: 纸币在中国有很长的历史。

items.en: It was first used during the Song Dynasty and made trading much easier.
items.zh: 它最早在宋朝使用，让交易变得方便多了。

items.en: Nowadays, we seldom use paper money!
items.zh: 现在我们很少用纸币了！

items.en: We use credit cards and digital currency more and more.
items.zh: 我们越来越多地使用信用卡和数字货币。

items.en: That’s right!
items.zh: 没错！

items.en: By learning history, we can understand how things change.
items.zh: 通过学习历史，我们能理解事物是如何变化的。

items.en: Visiting a history museum is a great way to learn more about ancient Chinese currency.
items.zh: 参观历史博物馆是更多了解中国古代货币的好方法。

items.en: I agree!
items.zh: 我同意！

items.en: Li Lin, let’s plan a museum visit soon.
items.zh: 李琳，我们尽快安排一次博物馆参观吧。

items.en: What do you do with your money?
items.zh: 你会怎么花自己的钱？

items.en: Everyone makes their own choices.
items.zh: 每个人都有自己的选择。

items.en: Here’s a great example of what to do with money.
items.zh: 下面就是一个很好的用钱例子。

items.en: Ma Xu realised another dream at age 86 by donating 10 million yuan of her life savings to her hometown, Mulan County.
items.zh: 马旭在86岁时又实现了一个梦想：她把1000万元一生积蓄捐给了家乡木兰县。

items.en: The donation was made up of earnings from scientific research and patent transfers.
items.zh: 这笔捐款来自科研收入和专利转让所得。

items.en: Ma was born in a doctor’s family in Mulan County.
items.zh: 马旭出生在木兰县的一个医生家庭。

items.en: She joined the PLA as a doctor in 1947.
items.zh: 1947年，她参军成为一名军医。

items.en: After many years of hard learning and training, she became China’s first female paratrooper in 1961.
items.zh: 经过多年刻苦学习和训练，她在1961年成为中国第一位女伞兵。

items.en: Ma and her husband put their hearts into research.
items.zh: 马旭和丈夫全身心投入研究。

items.en: They have gotten two invention patents and published more than 100 papers.
items.zh: 他们获得了两项发明专利，发表了一百多篇论文。

items.en: Ma has also developed many traditional Chinese medical prescriptions.
items.zh: 马旭还研制了许多中药方剂。

items.en: Now, they live a very simple life in a small house in Wuhan.
items.zh: 现在，他们住在武汉一间小房子里，生活非常简朴。

items.en: They still use the same hard bed from the 1970s and their sofas are over 50 years old.
items.zh: 他们还在用20世纪70年代的硬板床，沙发也已用了50多年。

items.en: They usually wear their military uniforms.
items.zh: 他们通常穿着军装。

items.en: Ma misses her hometown very much.
items.zh: 马旭非常想念家乡。

items.en: In 2018, they decided to donate all their savings to Mulan County.
items.zh: 2018年，他们决定把全部积蓄捐给木兰县。

items.en: Ma believes that better education can change lives.
items.zh: 马旭相信，更好的教育能改变人生。

items.en: She is happy to help teenagers in her hometown with her savings.
items.zh: 她很乐意用自己的积蓄帮助家乡的青少年。

items.en: True happiness can be found not in material things, but in the ability to make a difference in the lives of others.
items.zh: 真正的幸福不在物质里，而在于有能力改变他人的生活。

items.en: Can anyone tell me what money is and why we use it?
items.zh: 谁能告诉我钱是什么，我们为什么用它？

items.en: Money is something we use to buy things.
items.zh: 钱是我们用来买东西的东西。

items.en: It’s also something we get through work.
items.zh: 它也是我们通过工作得到的东西。

items.en: That’s right!
items.zh: 说得对！

items.en: Money is a medium of exchange.
items.zh: 钱是一种交换媒介。

items.en: It means we can trade it for goods and services.
items.zh: 意思是我们可以用它换取商品和服务。

items.en: Just imagine how difficult life would be without money.
items.zh: 想想看，要是没有钱，生活会有多难。

items.en: Do you think money is important?
items.zh: 你们觉得钱重要吗？

items.en: Yes, it helps us buy the things we need, like food and clothes.
items.zh: 重要，它能帮我们买需要的东西，比如食物和衣服。

items.en: Without money, it would be hard to afford those things.
items.zh: 没有钱，这些东西就很难买得起。

items.en: Exactly.
items.zh: 没错。

items.en: Money also helps us achieve our goals, like going to college or travelling.
items.zh: 钱还能帮我们实现目标，比如上大学或旅行。

items.en: And it allows us to help others and make a positive difference in the world.
items.zh: 它还能让我们帮助别人，给世界带来积极的改变。

items.en: I agree with everyone.
items.zh: 我同意大家的看法。

items.en: However, there are many things that are even more valuable than money.
items.zh: 不过，还有很多东西比钱更宝贵。

items.en: Can you give me some examples?
items.zh: 你们能举些例子吗？

items.en: Good health, happiness, and love.
items.zh: 健康、快乐和爱。

items.en: Family and knowledge.
items.zh: 家庭和知识。

items.en: Peace and friendship.
items.zh: 和平与友谊。

items.en: Excellent.
items.zh: 很好。

items.en: While money is important, it cannot buy everything.
items.zh: 虽然钱很重要，但它买不到一切。

items.en: Use money wisely and responsibly.
items.zh: 要明智、负责地用钱。

items.en: Always be grateful for what you have and share what you can.
items.zh: 永远感恩你所拥有的，并尽力分享。

items.en: Emma was excited when she heard about a big sale at a store near her home.
items.zh: Emma 听说家附近一家商店在大促销，很兴奋。

items.en: Everything was 20% off, and she wanted to go shopping with her mum, Mrs Carson.
items.zh: 所有商品都打八折，她想和妈妈 Carson 太太一起去购物。

items.en: Mrs Carson asked Emma what she wanted to buy, but Emma wasn’t sure yet.
items.zh: Carson 太太问 Emma 想买什么，但 Emma 还没想好。

items.en: She saw a pretty cotton dress, a nice blouse, and some cool shoes.
items.zh: 她看到一条漂亮的棉布连衣裙、一件好看的上衣和一双很酷的鞋。

items.en: However, her mum reminded her that she already had enough clothes.
items.zh: 不过，妈妈提醒她，她的衣服已经够多了。

items.en: “You already have so many blouses, Emma.
items.zh: “Emma，你的上衣已经那么多了。

items.en: I don’t think you need any more,” Mrs Carson said.
items.zh: 我觉得你不需要再买了，”Carson 太太说。

items.en: Disappointed, Emma thought for a moment and said, “They used to be very expensive, but now they’re cheap...”
items.zh: Emma 有些失望，想了想说：“它们以前很贵，现在却便宜了……”

items.en: Mrs Carson smiled and explained, “It’s not just about the price, Emma.
items.zh: Carson 太太笑了笑，解释道：“Emma，这不只是价格的问题。

items.en: We should spend money wisely.
items.zh: 我们应该明智地花钱。

items.en: Before buying something, we should consider our needs and wants.”
items.zh: 买东西之前，应该考虑我们的需要和想要。”

items.en: Curious to learn more, Emma asked, “What do you mean by needs and wants, Mum?”
items.zh: Emma 很好奇，问道：“妈妈，你说的需要和想要是什么意思？”

items.en: Patiently, Mrs Carson explained, “Needs are things that we must have, like food, clothes, and a safe home.
items.zh: Carson 太太耐心地解释：“需要是我们必须拥有的东西，比如食物、衣服和安全的家。

items.en: Wants, on the other hand, are things that we desire but can live without.
items.zh: 而想要，是我们渴望拥有、但没有也能生活的东西。

items.en: It’s important to make smart choices with our money.”
items.zh: 用钱做出明智的选择很重要。”

items.en: Emma started to realise how important it was to manage money wisely.
items.zh: Emma 开始意识到，明智地理财有多重要。

items.en: By understanding the difference between needs and wants, she knew that she could make better decisions about money.
items.zh: 明白了需要和想要的区别，她知道自己能对钱做出更好的决定。

items.en: Mary and her cousins would go every month for a big family meal at their grandparents’ house.
items.zh: Mary 和表兄弟姐妹每个月都会去祖父母家吃一顿丰盛的家庭聚餐。

items.en: Their grandfather often gave them a few coins, saying, “You can buy yourself something.”
items.zh: 祖父常常给他们几枚硬币，说：“你们可以给自己买点东西。”

items.en: Then all of them ran off to spend the money.
items.zh: 然后他们都跑开去花钱了。

items.en: The grandparents, aunts, uncles, and parents thought this was not good — the children would never learn to manage their pocket money.
items.zh: 祖父母、姑姑叔叔和父母都觉得这样不好——孩子们永远学不会管理零花钱。

items.en: So they decided to have a test.
items.zh: 于是他们决定做一次测试。

items.en: They wanted to see what the children could get with the coins within a year.
items.zh: 他们想看看孩子们一年内能用这些硬币换来什么。

items.en: Tom, the smallest kid, spent all his money on sweets.
items.zh: 最小的孩子 Tom 把所有的钱都花在了糖果上。

items.en: Jim was strong-willed.
items.zh: Jim 很有意志力。

items.en: He wanted to win the test.
items.zh: 他想赢得测试。

items.en: He saved every cent.
items.zh: 他一分钱都存了下来。

items.en: He was the clear winner.
items.zh: 他显然是赢家。

items.en: Then there was Mary.
items.zh: 然后是 Mary。

items.en: She loved the violin, but the family couldn’t pay for her violin lessons.
items.zh: 她喜欢小提琴，但家里付不起她的琴课费。

items.en: So Mary went to her neighbour, a violinist.
items.zh: 于是 Mary 去找邻居，一位小提琴手。

items.en: Mary offered him all the coins, asking the violinist to teach her how to play.
items.zh: Mary 把所有的硬币都给了他，请他教自己拉琴。

items.en: It wasn’t much money, but seeing Mary’s excitement, the violinist agreed.
items.zh: 钱并不多，但看到 Mary 那么兴奋，小提琴手答应了。

items.en: He taught her happily for months.
items.zh: 他愉快地教了她好几个月。

items.en: Later, the two played together in the park.
items.zh: 后来，两人一起在公园里演奏。

items.en: They were very successful, and Mary was able to buy her own violin.
items.zh: 他们非常成功，Mary 也买得起自己的小提琴了。

items.en: Years later, Mary became a very famous violinist.
items.zh: 多年后，Mary 成了一位非常著名的小提琴家。

items.en: From ancient times when a cow could be traded for a horse, to the 21st century when that same horse might easily be bought with a bank card, humans have always needed a way to buy and sell things at an agreed price.
items.zh: 从古代用一头牛换一匹马，到21世纪用银行卡就能轻松买下同样一匹马，人类一直需要一种按约定价格买卖东西的方式。

items.en: A system, like trading a cow for a horse, is called a barter system.
items.zh: 像用牛换马这样的制度，叫作以物易物制度。

items.en: It worked well for a long time.
items.zh: 它在很长一段时间里运行良好。

items.en: However, things became more complicated as the population rose.
items.zh: 然而，随着人口增长，事情变得更复杂了。

items.en: The daily life in such a world required a standard unit to measure the value of one thing against another.
items.zh: 在这样的世界里，日常生活需要一个标准单位来衡量一件东西相对于另一件东西的价值。

items.en: The era of money soon followed.
items.zh: 货币时代很快随之到来。

items.en: And it has been with us ever since.
items.zh: 从那以后，它一直伴随着我们。

items.en: Chinese people were the first to move from the bartering era to the money era.
items.zh: 中国人最早从以物易物时代进入货币时代。

items.en: They began to trade shells for the products they wanted as early as 3,000 years ago.
items.zh: 早在3000年前，他们就开始用贝壳交换自己想要的物品。

items.en: Hundreds of years later, the Chinese began to use copper and bronze to replace the shells.
items.zh: 几百年后，中国人开始用铜和青铜取代贝壳。

items.en: According to research, the world’s first paper money, jiaozi, appeared in Chengdu in 1023.
items.zh: 据研究，世界上最早的纸币“交子”于1023年出现在成都。

items.en: In ancient Europe, around the 6th or 5th century BCE, money coins came into use.
items.zh: 在古代欧洲，大约公元前6世纪或5世纪，钱币开始使用。

items.en: Unlike the Chinese, Europeans used precious metals such as gold and silver for their coins.
items.zh: 与中国不同，欧洲人用金银等贵金属铸造钱币。

items.en: Around the 17th century, paper money started to become more popular in Europe, because it was much easier to carry around and store.
items.zh: 大约在17世纪，纸币在欧洲开始变得更流行，因为它更容易携带和保存。

items.en: This system worked until the early 19th century when the Bank of England introduced “gold-backed” paper money.
items.zh: 这种制度一直延续到19世纪初，英格兰银行推出了“金本位”纸币。

items.en: If someone had this paper money, they could exchange it for a certain amount of gold or silver in the bank.
items.zh: 如果有人持有这种纸币，就可以在银行把它兑换成一定数量的黄金或白银。

items.en: This made people feel more secure because the paper money was connected to something valuable.
items.zh: 这让人们更有安全感，因为纸币与某种有价值的东西联系在了一起。
